question.text: Who is a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) and what additional measures does IFSCA require when a customer or beneficial owner is a PEP?

answer.text: A PEP is an individual entrusted with prominent public functions; IFSCA requires additional measures/enhanced CDD when a customer, beneficial owner, beneficiary, or beneficiary's BO is a PEP
A PEP is any person who has been convicted of a financial crime; they require EDD because they are known offenders
A PEP is a person who holds more than five bank accounts; they require EDD because multiple accounts indicate suspicious activity
A PEP is any person who has made political donations; they require EDD because political donations may be linked to money laundering

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the IFSCA workbook (p.76), a PEP is an individual who is or has been entrusted with prominent public functions (e.g., heads of state, senior politicians, senior government/judicial/military officials). Page 103 requires additional measures / enhanced CDD when a customer, beneficial owner, beneficiary, or beneficiary's BO is identified as a PEP. The Trap: Option B confuses PEPs with convicted criminals. PEP designation is based on the position of public function held, not on criminal history — many PEPs are entirely legitimate, but their position warrants enhanced scrutiny under IFSCA rules. Note: PEP status extends beyond the direct customer — screening should cover beneficial owners, beneficiaries, and a beneficiary's beneficial owner, with additional/enhanced measures applied at the latest when the PEP status is identified.
